title: Silicon is a semiconductor used because it can be switched between conducting and not
summary: A semiconductor such as silicon conducts electricity better than an insulator and worse than a metal, and it can be made to do either.
body: OpenStax Physics says some materials sit between conductors and insulators in conductivity. They are called semiconductors. They can be made conductive under the right conditions, which can involve temperature, purity, and the force pushing electrons through them. Because that behavior can be controlled, they are used extensively in computer chips. Silicon is named as the most commonly used semiconductor. The page's figure shows a large gap in conducting ability between the three groups, even though the drawing is compressed. This card does not explain how a chip is built.
